page.layout: One printed page (right-hand page of an opening, page 49 of the scan). Running head at top centre; page number at top right. Main text in one column of running text with headings "Canon 4." and "Canon 5.". Two small marginal notes in the right margin beside the lower text, and one margin note at the bottom right beside the final lines. Lower-left: a catchword-free text end with a drop-cap "C" and a note-like "Ex-" line at bottom.

main_text.p: tus adeò immoderatè tulit, ut Ducatum Philippo Valesio eâ conditione donaret, ut primogenitus Regis Franciæ appellaretur Delphinus.
main_text.head: Canon 4.
Explicatio:
main_text.p: Familia Valesiorum extincta fuit in Henrico III. A. C. 1589. Regnum igitur jure Legis Salicæ translatum fuit ad stirpem Borbonicam, cujus tunc caput erat Henricus Rex Navarræ, dictus postea IV. sive Magnus. Ei successit Ludovicus XIII. & qui nunc rebus Galliæ præest Ludovicus XIV.
main_text.head: Canon 5.
main_text.p: Imperium Germaniæ à Francis ad Saxones; alternatim ab his ad Svevos; deinde ad diversas familias; denique ad Austriacos devenit.Germanicum Imperium, quod consideratur secundum

page.notes: The right-margin notes are small and partly cut off; "Germanicum Imperium, quod consideratur" and "Imperium, quod consideratur secundum" are my best reading. The bottom-right note ("Ex- / catur sc / gundū") is set in small type and only partly legible; the final word "gundū" is uncertain. The page is slightly skewed, so the line ends at the right are hard to confirm. The drop cap "C" at the bottom is not a heading. Lines of the left-hand page are not part of this scan.
